tei:titleStmt.tei:title: [Gebet] An den ersten Tagen des Laubhüttenfestes
[A prayer] on the first days of Sukkot by Fanny Neuda (1855)

tei:div.tei:head: [Gebet] An den ersten Tagen des Laubhüttenfestes

tei:lg.tei:l: Prayer for the First Day of Sukkot
You shall celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days. (Deuteronomy 16:13)

Once again, a feast has come upon us—a feast quite different from the one we celebrated only recently. That one we celebrated with tears and acts of penance, with self-mortification and deprivation; this one we celebrate with joy, jubilation, and songs of praise, as it is written: “And you shall rejoice before the Eternal, your Lord, for seven days.” And how could cheerfulness and joy not fill our hearts, how could holy joy not fill our souls, now that this very feast has been preceded by the Feast of Atonement, and now that you, my God, have taken away our guilt and set us free from our sins! How could our minds, weighed down by the awareness of guilt, have opened themselves to a ray of joy if you had not extended your reconciling hand to us and blotted out our names from the book of guilt? Yet you have not only reconciled us, not only removed the well-deserved punishment from our heads, but in love and kindness you have turned your face toward us once more. Not as a master forgives a servant, but as a kind father takes his repentant child back into his arms, presses him to his heart once more, and cherishes him again with love and mercy—so do you, Almighty Father, deal with us in your divine grace. And so we rejoice and are glad before You, my God, and with joyful, comforted hearts we enter the festive tent that we have built and adorned in honor of Your commandment, and from purified hearts our prayer rises up to You.

In huts we celebrate the Feast of Sukkot, just like a nomadic people, just like our forefathers in the wilderness, who lived in huts during their journey. What a beautiful period in the life of our people this was!—Great through Your wonders and blessed by Your love, our forefathers camped in the free, open wilderness, yet Your grace hovered around them and above them, protecting them from every lurking enemy, from every danger and hardship; a pillar of cloud was their protection by day, a pillar of fire by night; the barren rock became a fresh, refreshing spring for them, food descended for them from the cloud, their feet walked unscathed across the scorching ground, and their garments did not tear until they entered the promised, praised land, which you had promised them as an inheritance and possession.

And has not Your divine, miraculous power been revealed to us time and again ever since? Have You not continually spread the shield and shelter of Your grace, and spread the wings of Your favor over the heads of Your people wherever the enemy’s power threatened to destroy them! For millennia, Israel has been a wandering people on earth; we journeyed toward the east and toward the west, and everywhere the ground beneath us became a hot and scorching desert; every fresh spring was closed to us; fragile huts, merely precarious and unstable, were our dwellings, which the harshness of time and the hatred and prejudice of the nations often enough brought crashing down upon our heads. “It is only by Your grace that we have not perished.” Your mercy has sustained and carried us across rivers and floods, across every abyss that threatened to swallow us up. And now, after a long journey, you have let us taste the sweetness of home! Thanks to you, we have a healthy homeland—a beautiful, glorious land that recognizes us as its children; the wandering tent of the stranger, the tolerated one, has been transformed into the firm, permanent dwelling place of the native and the native-born; safe and undisturbed, like Israel once in the shade of its palm and fig trees, we rest under the tent of peace that is the Law, just like all our brothers in the land.

Therefore, be praised, Lord, for the wonders You once performed for our fathers, and for the wonders You continue to perform for us, their children, even today! You have not forsaken us, nor will You forsake us. Praised and blessed be Your holy name. אָמֵן Amen.

tei:note.tei:p: Lamentations 3:22. Here, Neuda is referring to her native Bohemia.
